properties.Name: I-95
properties.WhyShort: Built in the middle of Jackson Ward cutting it in half and disrupting many homes and businesses. Displaced thousands of people
properties.WhyLong: In the 1950s, I-95 bisected Second Street and Jackson Ward as a whole. A block wide path was carved through the ward displacing an estimated 1,000 households and destroying hundreds of historic homes, buildings, and neighborhood structures. With construction ending in 1958, disruptions to the neighborhood were far from over. Today, about 150,000 cars per day drive along this portion of I-95 creating constant noise pollution. Along with this, the Northern section of Jackson Ward continues to be cut off from Historic Jackson Ward with less access to businesses and services.

properties.Name: Maggie Walker Historic Site
properties.WhyShort: First Black woman to charter and serve as President of a bank in the United States
properties.WhyLong: Opening in 1978, the Maggie L. Walker National Historic Site is the country’s first national park devoted to an African American woman. Maggie Walker was the first American woman to establish and head a bank.Along with this, Walker was the founder and president of the Richmond Council of Colored Women and worked to improve health care for African Americans. The historic site is preserved and furnished exactly how Maggie Walker left it.

properties.Name: Giles B. Jackson Law Office
properties.WhyShort: During the 1970s, Giles B Jackson's old office helped for the push for Jackson Ward's National Historic District Status
properties.WhyLong: Giles B. Jackson was born September 10, 1853 in Goochland County Virginia. Throughout his life, Jackson became an attorney, entrepreneur, real estate developer, newspaper publisher, and civil rights activist.  On November 30 1887 he became the first African American certified to practice law before the Virginia Supreme Court of Appeals. Jackson helped establish the Savings Bank of the Grand Fountain of the United Order of the True Reformers. In 1901 President Theodore Roosevelt commissioned Jackson as an honorary colonel. Jackson practiced law out of an office located on Second Street which helped the neighborhood get a National Historic District status.

properties.Name: Slaughter's Hotel
properties.WhyShort: Despite I-95 and all that happened, Slaughter's Hotel remained a vital part of the community through the 1970s.
properties.WhyLong: Slaughter’s Hotel was first opened by Richard Slaughter around 1924. By 1931 the hotel moved to a larger location across the street. Slaughter’s was well known for its dedication to high quality food and accommodations for Black travelers at a time when options were limited. From the 1930s-1940s the hotel was a prominent establishment that attracted lots of notable guests such as Oliver Hill. Gertrude Taylor took over hotel management in 1945 after Richard Slaughter passed away. Under Taylor’s management the hotel thrived as a gathering place for organizations such as the NAACP and the Richmond Crusade of Voters. Along with this, the hotel also served as a meeting place for political, social, and community leaders. Through the 1970s the hotel continued to be a staple with its club sandwich becoming a local legend. In the early 1990s the hotel was demolished to make way for the Jackson Center.
